title: Sam Burke's faith in him, starting at forty-five
summary: His career really started at 45; Jones credits his manager Sam Burke, who believed in a nearly finished trumpeter and told him he could not make people buy the records alone.

bands.name: Booker T. Washington Community Center Band

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: When I first come out of the Sunday school band, I first left, I said when I'm 40 years old I'm coming out of it. I thought that was old. Then I didn't get started till I was 45. I didn't get started till I was 45. But the great thing about it, let me say this about Sam Burke, that is the man. He did everything. He guided everything for me, right or wrong, right or wrong. I'm still with him, you know. I just listen to him, you know, because he did so much for me.
He had faith in you and he --

Yeah, a guy that'd have that much faith in you, you know. I was a trumpet player. Let's face it, I was a trumpet player out there, you know, and almost through, you know, and here's a guy come by and has enough confidence in me, and I was able. Of course I had something to do with it. Because he'd tell me that in a minute, 'I couldn't do it unless you did it.'
Unless you can deliver, you know. He said, 'I couldn't make them buy them records, you know.'
I think it was great that Cab gave you that advice. I really think that was very good.
